translation_notes: no @prefix declared: RDF/XSD are imported by original.py but never dereferenced in this 10-line body (they are read by the sibling operator functions in the same source file, not by Builtin_STRSTARTS) -- keeping the unused Python import for surface parity, per INSTRUCTIONS.md, without inventing an @prefix that would never be used

the coercion_datatype site is `Literal(a.startswith(b))`: no explicit datatype=, so it relies on rdflib's own default inference for a bare Python bool (xsd:boolean, lexical 'true'/'false') -- `f{a.startswith(b)}` goes through the language's `node()` coercion, which is documented to apply that same default inference, and empirically verified equal on both outcomes (see driver.py)

context shim (context_shim.py): `_compatibleStrings` (and the `string` helper it calls) live outside the extracted 10 lines, at lines 309-315/1017-1026 of the same source file -- both are themselves plain vendored rdflib code (rdflib.plugins.sparql.operators, copied unmodified into recipe-importer/), reproduced verbatim from LexMalta/recipes@b861b7ccea rather than paraphrased

expr/ctx: `expr` stands for whatever rdflib's SPARQL evaluator passes at the real call site -- an object exposing `.arg1`/`.arg2` (already-evaluated Literal terms). Only those two attributes are read here, so the driver uses a plain SimpleNamespace rather than constructing a real rdflib.plugins.sparql.parserutils.Expr (which needs a parsed CompValue). `ctx` is never read in this region and is passed as None throughout

anti-hollow-green (INSTRUCTIONS.md): changed `f{a.startswith(b)}` to `f{not a.startswith(b)}` in translated.ldpy -- rdfeval check correctly failed on all three calls (values differ, true vs false each time); reverted, check green again
